newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SHARKS, CAPITALS, COYOTES NAME NEW HEAD COACHES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SHARKS, CAPITALS, COYOTES NAME NEW HEAD COACHES.

text.p: Three National Hockey League teams - the San Jose Sharks, the Washington Capitals and the Phoenix Coyotes - named new head coaches on Monday.
The Coyotes announced Jim Schoenfeld will replace Don Hay, who was fired on May 6 after just one season behind the bench.
Schoenfeld, who himself was fired by the Capitals last week, was replaced in Washington by former Mighty Ducks of Anaheim coach Ron Wilson.
San Jose, who finished with the worst record in the Western Conference this season, named Darryl Sutter their new head coach.
Less than a week after being let go as head coach of the Capitals, Schoenfeld was back in the NHL with Phoenix Monday.

Schoenfeld, a rugged former NHL defenceman, was fired by the Capitals after the team failed to make the playoffs for the first time in 14 years. He guided Washington to a 33-40-9 record and a fifth-place finish in the Atlantic Division.
In eight seasons as an NHL head coach with Buffalo, New Jersey and Washington, Schoenfeld owns a 182-180-54 record.

The Coyotes, who moved to Phoenix last season after 17 years in the NHL as the Winnipeg Jets, finished fifth in the Western Conference with a 38-37-7 record last season and were ousted in the opening round of the playoffs by the Mighty Ducks.
Wilson, who was fired by the Disney-owned Anaheim team after losing in the playoffs to eventual Stanley Cup champions the Detroit Red Wings, becomes the new Capitals coach.

He coached the United States to victory in the World Cup last year and guided Anaheim to its first-ever playoff berth this season. The Mighty Ducks compiled a 36-33-13 record this season and finished in fifth place in the Western Conference.
He was the only coach the Mighty Ducks had, amassing a 120-145-31 record in four years with Anaheim.
The Capitals also named former Vancouver Canucks vice president of hockey operations George McPhee as the club's new general manager.
In San Jose, the Sharks said former Chicago Blackhawks coach would be their new coach.
He compiled a 110-80-26 record before leaving Chicago after the 1995 season for family reasons. Sutter also played for the Blackhawks from 1979-87, and was captain from 1982-87.

San Jose, which finished the season with a 27-47-8 record, fired coach Al Sims on May 9. The Sharks missed the playoffs for the second consecutive season after reaching the Western Conference semifinals in 1994 and 1995.
The Sharks have yet to record a winning season since joining the league in the 1991-92 season.
